S01: Once, beside the river Weser, lay the small town of Hamelin.
S02: One morning the town awoke beset by rats.
S03: They were everywhere: in the storerooms, in the kitchens, even beside the food.
S04: They even came to the children's cradles.
S05: The people stood before the doors, frightened and powerless.
S06: And the mayor was desperate: he wrung his hands and bewailed his fate.
S07: Mayor: "A thousand gold coins to whoever saves us from this plague!"
S08: Several days passed, and no one came.
S09: Then at the gate appeared a strange, slender silhouette.
S10: Piper: "I shall free Hamelin of the rats... but in exchange I want a thousand gold coins."
S11: Mayor: "Agreed! Do it, and you shall have all you wish!"
S12: And so, with a handshake, the bargain was struck.
S13: In the morning the piper stepped out into the middle of the square.
S14: And he began to play a strange, melodious tune.
S15: The sound of the pipe spread through the streets like a warm wind.
S16: In the dark burrows the rats pricked up their ears.
S17: One by one, they came out of the shadows.
S18: The rats, as if enchanted, gathered around the piper.
S19: The people watched, frozen, from the windows.
S20: The piper led them toward the town gate.
S21: The gate opened wide before them.
S22: He led them out, along the road that runs to the river.
S23: Their eyes were empty and bright, as if blinded by the music.
S24: On the very bank, the piper did not cease to play.
S25: And then, as one, they all hurled themselves into the swift water.
S26: In a few minutes not a single rat remained in Hamelin.
S27: And proudly he made his way to the town hall to claim his promised reward.
S28: But in the hall awaited him a very different reception.
S29: Piper: "I have come for my thousand gold coins."
S30: Mayor: "Be gone from here, wretched beggar! I will never pay that!"
S31: In the piper's eyes a cold ember flared.
S32: The door of the hall slammed shut behind him.
S33: And he, in silence, raised the instrument once more.
S34: Then he played again — but this time with another, sadder tune.
S35: The children raised their heads, and their eyes lit up.
S36: Laughing, they came out into the street and followed the sound.
S37: And all the little children followed the piper to the gate.
S38: The mothers and fathers, with horror, realized what was happening.
S39: Only one small child lagged behind and could not keep up the pace.
S40: The desperate parents sought help from the mayor.
S41: But his voice stuck in his throat.
S42: The children followed the piper deep into the forest.
S43: And they stopped before the entrance of an enormous cave.
S44: Then the little child finally caught up and threw himself at the piper's feet.
S45: Little child: "I beg you... do not take us away!"
S46: And the piper, who had a good heart, bent down to him.
S47: Piper: "You keep it playing, stubborn child. I gift it to you. Come, let everyone return home."
S48: And so the children turned back, home, to their parents.
S49: At the gate, sighs and laughter — every child found an embrace.
S50: And from that day, Hamelin always kept its promises. Of the strange piper, no one ever heard again.
